subject: Private deployment: geofencing, subprocessor disclosure, and customer KMS handoff
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@novabio.com>, NovaBio Legal <legal@novabio.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: geofencing, subprocessor disclosure, and customer KMS handoff

Hi Daniel / NovaBio legal team,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. Per our discussion, we wanted to confirm a few items so Redwood can produce a clean DPA addendum and an operational handoff checklist for the private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway) where NovaBio will manage encryption keys via a customer-controlled KMS. High-level asks below:

1) Subprocessor disclosure and timing
- NovaBio asked for full visibility into downstream subprocessors involved in on-prem support, telemetry (agent updates), and breakout services (monitoring/metrics). Can you confirm whether you need a committed list in the DPA itself or a notification window (e.g., 30 days before onboarding)?

2) Data geofencing and egress guarantees
- We proposed geofencing to EU-only processing for EU tenant data and explicit egress blocks outside the region. Please confirm which NovaBio environments require hard geofences vs. soft policy/configuration.

3) Customer KMS handoff and operator roles
- For the customer-controlled keystore, we plan an operator demarcation where Redwood will never hold key material. There are two operational exceptions we discussed: a) break-glass recovery invoked by NovaBio, and b) signed, auditable agent updates that may require a short-lived envelope key. Please confirm acceptance of that pattern and any legal/technical constraints.

4) Audit evidence and retention
- NovaBio requested evidence of access attempts, operator ACL changes, and telemetry uploads for 12 months. We typically provide audit logs and a signed integrity report. Are there additional artifacts you need for compliance?

Attachments: NovaBio_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (initial redlines), redline_subprocessors_list.csv (current list we maintain)

Next steps: if you can respond to the three points above and flag any mandatory contract language, we will:
- Produce an updated DPA addendum with geofence language and subprocessor notification cadence.
- Draft an operational KMS handoff playbook and runbook for review.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: NovaBio_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (pdf, 320KB)]

---

From: Daniel Park <dpark@novabio.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaBio Legal <legal@novabio.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: geofencing, subprocessor disclosure, and customer KMS handoff

Mina,

Appreciate the summary — this captures most of it. A few clarifications from NovaBio:

- Subprocessors: we need a committed list in the DPA for any subprocessor that will have the ability to read telemetry or manage agents in our environment. For purely distribution or non-sensitive monitoring, a 30-day notification is OK. The CSV you attached looks helpful but we will mark items that require 'committed' status.

- Geofencing: EU tenant data must be enforced by hard geofence (no allowed egress outside EU regions). For our US research cluster, soft policy is acceptable.

- KMS handoff: we accept the envelope pattern but require the break-glass process to be a documented, customer-initiated flow with signed approval from two NovaBio approvers. Also need confirmation that any short-lived envelope keys are audited and rotated on a 24-hour window.

- Audits: 12 months retention is fine, but we also require weekly signed integrity digests during the first 90 days post-deployment.

We attached our annotated DPA in-line as a Doc (see attached).

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Infrastructure
NovaBio
[Attachment: NovaBio_DPA_comments.docx (docx, 120KB)]

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: geofencing, subprocessor disclosure, and customer KMS handoff

Mina / Ben — forwarding Daniel's note and flagged asks. Quick internal notes below before we reply:

- Committed subprocessors: Legal prefers we keep the DPA to a committed list for anything that has administrative access to customer environments. For other telemetry vendors, a notification window is acceptable. We should propose a hybrid clause: a short annex listing committed subprocessors + a required 30-day notice for additions, with a customer right to object and request mitigation.

- Break-glass: engineering is comfortable with the signed two-approver flow. Need to confirm whether the approvers can be NovaBio service accounts or must be named individuals. Recommend we allow named approvers plus a service-account fallback only with explicit delegation recorded in the audit record.

- Envelope keys: we can implement 24-hour rotation and audit logging. Need to call out whether rotation is enforced by Redwood or by the NovaBio KMS (preferably NovaBio).

Action items for reply to NovaBio:
1) Draft hybrid subprocessor clause.
2) Draft KMS handoff runbook that includes the two-approver break-glass flow and 24-hour envelope key rotation details.
3) Confirm audit digest cadence and delivery channel (SFTP vs signed Drive manifest).

I'll draft a reply tomorrow morning.

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@novabio.com>, NovaBio Legal <legal@novabio.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: geofencing, subprocessor disclosure, and customer KMS handoff

Daniel / legal team — thanks for the clear asks. We ran this past engineering and legal and propose the following mutual action plan to keep timelines tight:

1) Next 3 business days: Redwood to produce
   - DPA addendum with hybrid subprocessor annex (committed list + 30-day notification + customer objection right).
   - KMS handoff runbook draft including: operator demarcation, two-approver break-glass flow, and envelope key rotation responsibilities (we will mark Noah (NovaBio) as approver placeholder but it can be replaced with a group/service account if you provide delegation records).

2) Within 5 business days: NovaBio to review and provide targeted redlines or accept the addendum.

3) Deployment gating: hard geofence enforcement for EU tenant(s) must be tested in staging and verified by NovaBio before production cutover.

We will attach the runbook and updated subprocessor annex to the DPA and circulate a single combined package via DocuSign for signatures. If that sounds good, can you confirm the two approvers for break-glass and whether you prefer SFTP or signed Drive manifests for weekly digests?

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability (on behalf of Operations)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PrivateDeploy_KMS_HandOff_Summary.docx (docx, 85KB)]
